- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment scores > 0.6) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for consecutive high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >80) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment dips below 0.4.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (days 1–7) — cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean-reversion bias in mid-horizon (days 8–15) — adjust downward if true outcome deviates >2% from 14-day moving average.
- Lagged overreaction in late horizon (days 16–30) — reduce forecast by 1–4% if sentiment is weak or sentiment history shows recent volatility.
- Avoid overconfidence in high sentiment + high price history — if sentiment > 0.7 and price > 80, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid “peak-predicted” bias.
